subject: Post-call: isolation playbook & next-step checklist
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: isolation playbook & next-step checklist

Liam — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed follow-ups so we can converge on whether Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) is the right path for Fintegrate. Keeping it short with concrete asks so we can move to a technical workshop.

Key points from call:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for PII-containing inference traffic (no cross-tenant co-mingling).
- Regulatory: must prove customer-managed key control (KMS/HSM) and auditability for requests and model inputs/outputs.
- Network: desire for zero public egress for production inference (no internet-accessible endpoints).
- SLA/availability: 99.9% target; ops runbook and failover behavior matter.

Questions we need clarified to recommend Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem: 
1) Data residency & egress: Will you accept a dedicated GPU pool in our managed Dedicated offering if we provide VPC peering + strict egress controls? Or do you require a Private deployment (control plane inside your VPC / on-prem) because of contractual egress prohibitions?
2) Key management: Is customer-managed KMS a hard requirement for all secrets and model keys, or only for persisted stored artifacts?
3) Audit & retention: What retention window do you need for request/response logs and how quickly must you be able to extract audit records for audits (e.g., 72 hours vs 30 days)?
4) Network topology: Are you ok with a minimal public control-plane with data plane in your VPC, or must the entire control plane be hosted in your environment?

Proposed immediate next steps (pick from 1-3):
- Technical workshop (60–90m) with your infra/security + our infra/ops to go over network diagrams, AWS account IDs, and KMS approach. (We recommend this.)
- Exchange a short MOP (method of procedures) doc and a sample deployment matrix (attached) so you can annotate where each requirement lands.
- Security questionnaire + SOC2 artifacts exchange — we can fast-track the SOC2 summary for your GRC team.

Attachments: redwood-deploy-matrix.xlsx (suggested decision matrix), sample-mop.pdf (example MOP).

If you confirm availability, we can schedule the workshop as early as Thursday. I’ll include Monica and Karthik to cover ops and architecture.

—
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@fintegrate.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@fintegrate.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: isolation playbook & next-step checklist

Sean — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications inline: 

1) Egress: Contractually, production inference payloads (both inputs and outputs) cannot leave our AWS accounts. That effectively rules out any managed-hosted option where payloads traverse vendor networks. We are open to Dedicated if the data plane lives in our VPC and there is NO network path from other customers into those instances.

2) KMS: Customer-managed KMS is a hard requirement for keys that encrypt persisted model artifacts and stored logs. For ephemeral request-level encryption in-transit, standard TLS is ok but we need proof that key lifecycle operations are under our control.

3) Audit retention: We need the ability to export raw audit logs for 12 months and have an ad-hoc export capability within 72 hours.

4) Control plane: Preferred is a hybrid: control plane can be managed but must have minimal visibility into raw payloads. If that isn’t feasible, we’ll require the control plane in our VPC.

Workshop: Thursday works for us — any time after 9:30am PT. We’ll bring our security architect (Aisha) and a networking engineer.

Thanks — will review your attachments and annotate.

—
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Security
Fintegrate Inc.
liam@fintegrate.com | +1 (212) 555-6412

Liam — quick technical questions to make the workshop efficient: 

- Do you have an existing AWS account ID(s) we can include in the VPC peering plan? If you prefer, provide a placeholder and we’ll make the diagrams generic.
- For customer-managed KMS, do you expect us to integrate with a cross-account key policy or deploy an HSM in your subnet? We can support both patterns, but we need to align on IAM roles and key access semantics ahead of the workshop.
- Are there specific CIDR ranges or strict NACL rules we should account for?

If you send the answers, we’ll pre-draft a network diagram and an initial IAM/key-access proposal so the technical meeting is focused.
